items.title: Why My Conversations with OpenAI’s ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ Made Me Very Worried
items.author: Brian X. Chen
items.content: <article>A new mode includes a study tool, but it still does a user’s homework. And a children’s safety nonprofit says the chatbot flunked its tests.</article>

items.title: Energy Firms Try to Squeeze More Power Out of Old Nuclear Plants
items.author: Brad Plumer and Rebecca F. Elliott
items.content: <article>It takes a long time to build new nuclear plants. So, some U.S. companies are looking to get more electricity out of reactors that already exist.</article>

items.title: Mixed Human Feelings After a Day at a Park Full of Robots
items.author: Yan Zhuang and Jiwoong Hong
items.content: <article>I went to Galaxy Robot Park in Seoul to see how we might one day live with robots. It was part cutting-edge technology, part theatrics.</article>

items.title: In Race With U.S., China Struggles to Recruit Foreign A.I. Researchers
items.author: Zeyi Yang
items.content: <article>China’s booming artificial intelligence sector has given local researchers good reason to remain in the country, but it has yet to lure overseas scientists despite a government push.</article>

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day Is Nostalgic With Rich Visuals
items.author: Christopher Byrd
items.content: <article>In Gears of War: E-Day, it’s fun to see the origins of beloved characters in grand scale, even if its play feels conservative.</article>

items.title: South Korea Investigates Possible Use of A.I. in Hackings on Its Banks
items.author: Laura Chung and Jin Yu Young
items.content: <article>The president said there were signs that such models were used in recent attacks on several banks involving customer data. Police are investigating.</article>

items.title: Court Tosses ​​Sentence After A.I. Video of Victim ‘Forgiving’ His Killer Is Played
items.author: Adeel Hassan
items.content: <article>An appellate court in Arizona threw out the prison sentence of a man convicted of manslaughter after an A.I.-generated video of his victim was played at a trial.</article>

items.title: US Solar Panel Makers Try to Catch China With a Big Leap in Technology
items.author: Ivan Penn and Patrick Junker
items.content: <article>Manufacturers say they are close to perfecting a new, more efficient solar panel that could help the United States reclaim ground it lost.</article>

items.title: Are Babies Conscious?
items.author: Carl Zimmer
items.content: <article>By pinpointing when it begins in young humans, scientists hope to better understand what consciousness is, and how it arises, in all of us.</article>

items.title: Inside Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao’s Life After Prison
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany
items.content: <article>Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.</article>
